draft.title: Debit and credit rules
card: Every account has a debit side (left) and a credit side (right). Whether a debit raises or lowers an account depends on the type of account.
assets and expenses. A credit decreases them.
liabilities, owner's equity and revenue. A debit decreases them.
Cash received from a customer for a sale: debit Cash (an asset rises) and credit Sales (revenue rises). Paying wages: debit Wages (an expense rises) and credit Cash (an asset falls).
draft.remember: Debit raises assets and expenses. Credit raises liabilities, owner's equity and revenue.

a.q: Which entry correctly records a business paying its electricity bill in cash?
a.why: Electricity is an expense, so it rises with a debit. Cash is an asset and falls, so it is credited. Debiting Cash would wrongly increase the cash held.
a.clue: An expense rises on the debit side, and cash goes out.

b.q: Priya's Bikes borrows $5,000 from a bank and the money is paid into its bank account. Which entry records this?
b.why: The bank account is an asset and rises, so it is debited. The loan is a liability and rises, so it is credited. Crediting Owner's equity is tempting because it also rises with a credit, but the money is borrowed and not put in by the owner.
b.clue: Is the money owed back to someone outside the business?
